abstracts.abstract: Software architecture erosion poses significant challenges to system maintainability and reliability, yet existing approaches fail to capture the dynamic interplay between architectural decay and software evolution. This paper introduces the Architecture-Behavior Co-Evolution (ABCE) framework, a novel paradigm that conceptualizes software architecture not as a static artifact but as a continuously evolving entity that co-evolves with system behavior and code structure. The ABCE framework integrates temporal dependency graphs, behavioral consistency metrics, and entropy-based erosion indicators to model the bidirectional relationship between architectural decisions and implementation changes. Through formal analysis of 47 open-source software systems spanning multiple domains, we demonstrate that architectural erosion follows predictable patterns that correlate with specific code smell accumulations and maintenance activity types. The framework enables proactive architecture health assessment by identifying erosion-prone components before critical failure points occur. Our evaluation reveals that the ABCE framework achieves 87.3% accuracy in predicting architectural decay trajectories, outperforming existing technical debt quantification methods by 34.2 percentage points. This paradigm shift from reactive to predictive architecture management represents a fundamental advancement in how software engineering practitioners conceptualize and address architectural sustainability.

Accurate software reliability prediction remains critical for release planning and resource allocation, yet current reliability growth models inadequately handle the non-homogeneous nature of defects discovered in modern agile development contexts. This paper presents an Enhanced Bayesian Reliability Model (EBRM) that substantially improves upon traditional exponential family models by incorporating failure severity classification, detection environment heterogeneity, and iterative development phase transitions. The proposed model extends the classical Goel-Okumoto framework through a hierarchical Bayesian structure that distinguishes between latent defect categories and their respective detection probabilities across sprint boundaries. We derive closed-form posterior distributions using variational inference approximation, enabling practical implementation without intensive computational resources. Empirical validation was conducted on 23 software projects from three different organizations, encompassing over 2.8 million test execution records. Results demonstrate that EBRM reduces prediction error by 41.7% compared to the NHPP-based models and 28.3% compared to existing Bayesian approaches. The model provides actionable insights for quality assurance resource allocation, with particular effectiveness in projects exhibiting non-monotonic failure rate patterns typical of continuous integration environments. Sensitivity analysis confirms robust performance across varying prior specifications.

Automated program repair has made significant strides in generating syntactic fixes, yet existing techniques predominantly operate in isolation from human-developed verification oracles and frequently produce implausible solutions that fail real-world deployment requirements. This paper presents VerifiRepair, a novel automated repair framework that integrates large language model capabilities with constraint-based verification oracles to generate semantically correct and deployment-ready patches. The system architecture comprises three novel components: (1) a context-aware patch generation engine leveraging fine-tuned code models, (2) a specification extraction module that mines implicit requirements from existing test suites and documentation, and (3) a semantic equivalence validator ensuring behavioral consistency between buggy and corrected versions. VerifiRepair processes candidate patches through iterative refinement, incorporating feedback from failed verification attempts to guide subsequent generation cycles. Evaluation on the Defects4J benchmark, comprising 395 bugs across 6 real-world projects, demonstrates that VerifiRepair achieves a test-based repair rate of 67.6%, compared to 43.2% for state-of-the-art genetic programming approaches. Notably, 89.4% of VerifiRepair-generated patches pass human expert review for plausibility, substantially reducing the semantic gap between automated repair and manual intervention. This work establishes a new paradigm for trustworthy automated software repair that prioritizes semantic correctness alongside syntactic validity.

Continuous integration environments generate vast volumes of test execution data, yet existing test prioritization techniques inadequately leverage historical failure patterns and code change characteristics to dynamically optimize regression test suites. This paper introduces TestFlow, an enhanced test prioritization system that substantially improves upon existing time-aware approaches through multi-dimensional failure prediction and adaptive prioritization scheduling. TestFlow incorporates three significant architectural innovations: (1) a deep learning-based failure prediction model trained on historical execution traces and code change embeddings, (2) a dynamic test clustering module that groups tests by shared dependencies and mutation sensitivity, and (3) a cost-aware scheduling algorithm that balances failure detection probability with execution time constraints. The system operates in real-time during CI pipeline execution, continuously adjusting test order based on incoming code changes and intermediate test results. We integrated TestFlow into the CI pipelines of four industrial software projects, conducting controlled experiments over a six-month period encompassing 15,247 CI builds. Results indicate that TestFlow achieves 23.4% reduction in fault detection delay and 31.8% reduction in average build time compared to existing coverage-based and history-based prioritization methods. The system scales effectively to large test suites exceeding 10,000 test cases while maintaining sub-second prioritization decision latency.
